title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The headline alone establishes that a lawyer practicing in Minnesota was suspended in connection with submitting case citations that were fabricated, and that an AI system was involved in producing those citations. This is a known failure mode in which a language model generates plausible-looking but nonexistent legal references, and a user submits them to a court without independently verifying that the cases exist. The failure occurred at the point of human review, or rather at the absence of it, because any check against an actual legal database would have exposed the citations as false before they reached a court.

The underlying model behavior is a system asserting invented information as fact, a pattern well documented when language models are asked to retrieve specific legal, scientific, or bibliographic sources. That behavior becomes consequential only when a professional does not treat the output as a draft requiring verification.

What the article establishes beyond the headline is not available here, because the full text was not provided. It is not established what AI tool was used, precisely how the citations were discovered to be false, or what the exact terms of the suspension were.
